cds.title: Skidmore College Common Data Set 2025-2026 (PDF, Institutional Research)

scorecard.title: College Scorecard (location, enrollment, cost; data released 2026-10-15)

stats.notes: Fall 2025 entering class, from the Common Data Set. Residency rows (in-state 2,636 / out-of-state 4,872 / international 4,765 applicants; 742 / 1,886 / 289 admitted; 233 / 410 / 49 enrolled) add up to the totals (12,273 / 2,917 / 692). C1 enrolled (692) is the count on the first day of classes; B1 shows 690 at the fall census. ED figures (847 applications, 359 admitted; ED I 446 and ED II 401 applications) exclude ED applicants who were deferred to the Regular Decision pool and admitted there, per the CDS footnote. Test scores are optional: 25% of enrolled first-years (171) submitted the SAT and 8% (57) the ACT. Skidmore did not report high school GPA (marked N/A) or a GPA distribution. Undergraduate enrollment (2,719: 2,691 full-time and 28 part-time) and the nonresident count (186) are from B1 and B2.

cost.notes: First-year, full-time costs for 2025-26 from the Common Data Set (G1, G5); the CDS ticks '2026-2027 costs not available' (final costs expected 6/1/2026). Tuition $69,210, required fees $1,370 for first-year students (includes a one-time $150 records fee for new students; $1,220 for other undergraduates), food and housing $18,820 (housing $11,130 + food $7,690). Estimated expenses for residents: books and supplies $1,300, transportation $300, other $1,350 (other costs shown = transportation + other). The CDS prints no total. Aid figures (H6): the college's need-based and non-need-based aid is available to nonresidents; 97 degree-seeking nonresidents received it, average $81,400 (total $7,900,000, as printed, rounded).
